speaker: freelancer
text: Stability will come from a solid base fitted with rubber/TPU feet, which should stop the unit from rattling or shifting. On the electronics side, the first build will stay as simple as possible and use off-the-shelf components. Selecting a motor that easily handles the liquid load should also make the mixing reliable. I could provide an initial BOM within 72-96 hours.

speaker: client
text:
This approach and timeline sound great, Nolan, so let’s move forward.

The first step should cover:
• system layout
• motor + component selection
• basic wiring plan

From there, the goal is to get a working prototype running as quickly as possible and refine it afterward. Tell me what information you need from me to begin.

speaker: client
text: Let’s adopt this design while retaining the DJ Turntables vibe. The pour spot should face the baristas, all buttons need to be functional, and splashing should be minimized as much as possible. Keep the existing words on the machine unchanged, apart from the title, which should read "Elena's Chai Whisk," and use green accents. I also want to retain the thickness shown in the side view. The matcha wells should be deep, but the box itself must not become too large.

speaker: client
text: For V1, what simple, reliable implementation approach would you use for the spout? It must provide a smooth, controlled pour while remaining easy to clean between uses. A proper seal should prevent liquid from leaking into the base, and the open/close mechanism needs to operate cleanly without dripping.

speaker: client
text:
Key Design Details

1\. Valve / flow control — I need a simple open/close valve or tap that prevents constant dripping and uncontrolled pouring.

2\. Seal at the bottom — This is critical: the bottom bowl seal must prevent external leaks as well as seepage into the electronics.

3\. Cleaning — Because matcha + milk leaves residue, the spout should either be removable or easy to flush and clean.

4\. Flow rate — I need a smooth, controlled stream rather than a slow drip or an explosive pour.

speaker: freelancer
text: Taking the recent design requirements into account, I’ve prepared the initial BOM for your review. Additional wires, hardware, and the custom-fabricated housing are not included yet, although I already have their materials in my shop; they will be added after the build begins. I’m now starting the initial cad design with rough component measurements. Once you approve and purchase the components, I can measure each physical piece accurately and fully refine the design. All components have been sourced from amazon so future changes or additions can be handled quickly.

speaker: freelancer
text: Power for the electronics comes from a 120v-to-12v 35A DC supply, with each station using its own PWM speed controller. At each station, a 12v 450rpm motor connects through a 1/2" shaft coupling to a 1/2" stainless steel shaft, which drives the wire whisk for mixing and frothing the matcha. The electronics are actively cooled by 80mm fans. In the plumbing system, every 4.5 quart stainless steel bowl has a 3/8 barb outlet, where a #5 silicone stopper creates a press-fit, leak-proof connection. From the barb union inside that stopper, 3/8 silicone tubing runs to the 1" ght adapter, which threads directly onto the push-style beverage spigot.

speaker: client
text: Could the spout be revised to match the diagram more closely? I’m unsure whether Matcha will retain the same consistency after running through the proposed spout, and it will not preserve the frothiness.

speaker: freelancer
text: Regarding the whisk, understood—I’ll source a more suitable option for that component. The spout shown in your image is possible, but reproducing it would require us to rethink the design, develop custom circuitry, and do additional custom work. To make matcha flow through that type of spout on demand, we would essentially need a solenoid that opens and closes a valve inside the dispensing mechanism. Developing a reliable solution would involve custom mechanical parts, wiring, and some R&D, so it would likely push us beyond the timeline for this 1st edition. Several off-the-shelf spout alternatives are available, though. Could one of those work instead?
